turns.prompt_text: Okay so I don't have it it I imagine I have it physically somewhere but I'm not going to be finding it anytime soon Is it illegal for me to have lost it? I imagine I could request it from the Texas local government or that specific automobile shop
turns.response_html:
No, it is not illegal to lose a bill of sale. There is no law that penalizes you simply for misplacing your copy of the paperwork.

However, losing it does create a liability risk. In Texas, a seller is supposed to file a Vehicle Transfer Notification (Form VTR-346) with the TxDMV within 30 days of a sale. If that notification wasn't filed, the vehicle technically remains in your name in the state system until the buyer registers it. This means you could be held responsible for parking tickets, toll violations, or impound fees if the vehicle is ever put back on the road.

If you want to track down proof of the sale to cover your bases, you have two main avenues:

1. Contact the Salvage Yard (Fastest Option)

Since San Antonio Truck & Equipment is a legitimate, large-scale commercial business, they are required to keep detailed accounting and inventory records—especially when acquiring vehicles for scrap or parts.

Reaching out to them directly is highly likely to yield results. You can call their main office, provide your name, the vehicle details (2001 Pontiac Grand Am), and the rough timeframe (early 2023), and ask if they can pull the transaction receipt or purchase agreement from their archives.

2. Request Records from the Texas DMV (TxDMV)

If the salvage yard properly filed the title transfer or a salvage certificate, the Texas DMV will have a record of it. You can formally request this information from the state, though it takes a bit more effort:

  • Form VTR-275: You need to fill out a "Request for Texas Motor Vehicle Information" form.
  • What to ask for: You can request a "Title History" for that specific vehicle (if you have the VIN) or request a "List of vehicles in your name" to see if the Grand Am is still legally attached to you.
  • How to submit: These specific requests cannot be done via email. You have to submit the form, a copy of your government-issued ID, and a small fee (usually around $2 to $5) either by mail or in person at a TxDMV Regional Service Center.

Since mailing a form from Iowa to Texas and waiting for processing will take weeks, giving the salvage yard a quick phone call is definitely your best first step.
